answer: Agents earn the right to trade only after locking a scarce deposit that can be slashed when an independent audit proves fraud. A newcomer’s claims are sampled against signed delivery receipts from counterparties; colluding accounts cannot create those receipts merely by multiplying identities. To attack at scale, an adversary must fund each identity and risk losing its bond, so the cost rises with the number of agents rather than with the cheapness of registration. This pulse of capital discipline works across an ocean of markets and a tundra of sparse activity.
